### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **15** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**17** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 66949b7729f33cd3624e2789b4205f583301ee6a`.

⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **144** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 66949b7729f33cd3624e2789b4205f583301ee6a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `829bedca828868402afc9157d11c853aa96ad54a` — the merge of head `b546c5ff20e1c8b8b3f5786af4e2f340175ed871` into base `66949b7729f33cd3624e2789b4205f583301ee6a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 829bedca828868402afc9157d11c853aa96ad54a && git checkout 829bedca828868402afc9157d11c853aa96ad54a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 66949b7729f33cd3624e2789b4205f583301ee6a b546c5ff20e1c8b8b3f5786af4e2f340175ed871 && git checkout -B drift-repro 66949b7729f33cd3624e2789b4205f583301ee6a && git merge --no-ff b546c5ff20e1c8b8b3f5786af4e2f340175ed871

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 66949b7729f33cd3624e2789b4205f583301ee6a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 66949b7729f33cd3624e2789b4205f583301ee6a` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `b546c5ff20e1c8b8b3f5786af4e2f340175ed871`
Local-runs: none

Reviewed on the PR head as read from the API (it equals the head the brief named; a draft of 14 commits over merge base `4f5679c26`, 14 files, +1157/−31, base `main`, head repo equal to base repo). Inputs: card #23165 (body; the first claim `6139885605`, the first dev report `6141156635`, the release `6141220035`, triage's direction `6141939797`, the claim `6142825996`, this round's report `6148282605`, the ACCEPT `6148342520`), PR #23290 (body, file list, its one docs-drift comment), #22128 with PR #22185 (body, files, its FAIL `6053073603` and PASS `6053978836` records), the net diff `origin/main...b546c5ff2`, `origin/main` for context (ADR-0070, ADR-0048 §3.3, `rest-server.ts`, `sys-metadata-repository.ts`, `protocol.zod.ts`, the changeset gates and the lock gate), and the head's check-runs. Nothing built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The one resolution, `packagelessAddress` (`protocol.ts`).** It reads the item's environment rows at the write's state, canonical type and bundle member, with no package predicate, through `engine.find` in full (never a `findOne`), and answers the one distinct binding, `null` for none or for two or more, and whether a package-unbound row sits beside them; an unprovisioned store is no binding, any other read failure propagates. No storage-order pick remains on either changed path: the save hands the resolved package to every gate below it, and the delete hands `packageId` (a string, or an explicit `null`) to `repo.get` and `repo.delete`, which resolve an explicit `null` as the exact unbound row (`'packageId' in opts`, unchanged on `main`), where before both were handed no key and took the repository's "any row" match. **Right**, and triage's direction (`6141939797`) is followed on both doors: one package names that row; two or more are refused `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT` naming them with nothing written or deleted; none keeps the unbound row as before.
2. **Save door, `PUT /meta/:type/:name` with no `?package=` (`packageId` absent or `null` in process), publish mode, no `source`, not `package-duplicate`.** Resolved once, below the code-only, package-door and `_lock` refusals (#22220's order), above the D9.9 object check, the stored lock family (`authoredLockFamily` at `:21430` reads `repo.headAt` at the resolved package), the writable-base check, the lock parent, the carry-forward, `repo.put` and the receipt. One bound package: the save writes that row, the item read serves it next, and the receipt reads `(env-wide, package=P, state=active)`. **Right**; pinned over the row-keeping stub engine (`protocol.packageless-save-address.test.ts`) and over the real routes on better-sqlite3 (`meta-draft-head-package-inheritance.test.ts`).
3. **Two packages, save.** Refused `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT`, both packages named and sorted, `?package=` the remedy, nothing written — the standard-catalog code this package already answers for a name several owners hold (`importUnmanagedPackage`), no ledger row minted. **Right**; pinned at both layers with `code` and `status` through `resolveThrownHttpError`.
4. **Every flipped request class on the save door is declared** (PR body line 2; the changeset's FROM, TO, "Also refused now" and "Remedy"): (a) a package-less save carrying the package row's `If-Match`: 409 → 200, the flip #22128 declared for the same shape; (b) `If-None-Match: *` on a package-owned item: 200 with a second row minted → `409 METADATA_CONFLICT`; (c) a package-less save of an item a read-only package holds: 200 with an orphan overlay → `422 WRITABLE_PACKAGE_REQUIRED`, what `?package=` naming it answers; (d) the package-less read's `version` for a one-package item: `null` → that row's token (`readVersionToken`, the active arm only; two packages keep the unbound row's token as the docblock says; the draft arm is unchanged); (e) an overlay row already bound to a code package: the package-less save writes it instead of minting the unbound overlay; (f) the save receipt gains `, package=P`. **Right.** The unbound item and the no-stored-row code-package item read byte for byte as before (pinned controls).
5. **Delete door, `DELETE /meta/:type/:name` with no `?package=`.** Resolved from the rows at the state it removes (a draft discard reads the draft rows, so the #11087-inherited draft is found), below the organization refusal, the origin-gated door, the packaged-base door and the `_lock` gate (`orgId` is `null` by construction, matching the resolution's environment-only read). One package: that row is removed and the served token is accepted as `parentVersion`. Two: refused 409, the door's own verdict rethrown as-is through the `catch`. None: the unbound row, receipt byte for byte. **Right**; pinned at both layers, the draft discard both ways.
6. **The widening.** `deleteMetaItem.packageId?: string | null`; `DeleteMetaItemRequestSchema.packageId` as `z.string().nullable().optional()`, the save's exact zod shape (`null` accepted, a non-string refused, pinned); REST `?package=` through `metaItemPackageBinding` (`all` and the empty value answer `undefined`, spread only when truthy — byte for byte the PUT door's spelling at `main:7160`), `package` added to `META_ITEM_RESET_PARAMS` and to the repeated-parameter guard, with a preservation pin (the request `deleteMetaItem` receives for a package id, `all` and empty) and a refusal pin (a repeated `?package=` is 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR`, protocol never called). **Necessary**: at base the delete named no package at any layer and the closed set refused `?package=` 400, so triage's ordered refusal would have named a remedy the door could not take, and an absence must be loud and name its remedy. **Proportionate**: one optional key, one closed-set member. **Right.**
7. **`deletePackage` and the draft discards.** `deletePackage` (`DeletePackageRequest.packageId: string`, required) now names its package on each row's delete; `discardDraftInItsScope` carries `d.packageId`, which `repo.listDrafts({ packageId })` answers as a string, for `discardPackageDrafts` and `revertStoredPackage`. At base each deleted by name through the repository's "any row" match, so for a name two packages hold it could remove the other package's row and keep its own; under the new refusal they would instead be refused outright. A real defect fix and a necessity, inside triage's delete-door direction and ADR-0070 TL;DR 4 (the package is the lifecycle unit). **Right**; pinned (an uninstall and a discard each remove only their own row).
8. **The receipt and the response docblock.** The active sentences claimed the item gone or back at artifact default; that was false at base whenever another row remained, and a named delete makes it reachable on purpose. Now a package row's delete names its package; when another row is still stored the receipt names it (packages sorted, at most five, the package-less row by name); a named package with no row answers `success: true, reset: false` naming what remains, and never reaches the registry heal; the unbound-row-nothing-left sentence is unchanged. The docblock's two `reset` sentences are true against the code. **Right**; the five probe readings in the PR body match the templates.
9. **The describes.** `SaveMetaItemRequestSchema.packageId`: each sentence holds against ①.2–4 (absent or `null` names none; one package → that row, as a save naming it; two → 409; none → the env-local overlay; the row written is the parent-version resolution's and the read's `version`). `DeleteMetaItemRequestSchema.packageId`: holds against ①.5–8, including "a package that holds no row removes nothing" and "that row is the one `parentVersion` is judged against" (`repo.delete` receives both). `protocol.mdx` is regenerated for both tables, `authorable-surface/api.json` gains its one row, and `check:docs` (Type Check · source gates) and `check:api-surface` (Type Check · consumer gates) are success on the head. **Right.**
10. **`SysMetadataRepository`'s `null` callers keep their meaning.** `sys-metadata-repository.ts` is not in the diff, so `put`, `headAt` and `delete` keep their documented defaults. The only `repo.put` site is `saveMetaItem`'s, and its in-protocol callers are three: `migrateStoredMetadata` (`source: 'migrate-stored'`, exempt by the `source` predicate, and pinned: `packageId: null` with a `source` still writes the unbound row), `duplicatePackage` (`writeFace: 'package-duplicate'`, names its target) and the unmanaged import (names its target). The draft save keeps `resolveWriteHead`: its two-package case is a storage-order bind the new function refuses, so folding it would not have been a pure refactor. **Right.**
11. **In-process package-less writers outside the diff inherit the resolution.** plugin-security's projection and write-through save and delete by name with no package, and the runtime's flow registration door (`packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts`, `registerAndSaveFlow`) saves `flow` package-less with no `source`. For a one-package item each now writes or removes the package's row where before it minted an orphan beside it or removed the first row met; for two packages each is refused 409 (the flow door relays the error and rolls the engine registration back). That is the ordered behaviour, a loud refusal in place of a silent misaddressed write: **right**. The report names plugin-security's and not the flow door's (③).
12. **The `_lock` gates.** The save door hands its caller-named package to `assertLockAllowsWrite`; the delete door's `assertLockAllowsDelete` has no `packageId` and hands none to `getEffectiveLock`, which accepts one. The overlay lock layer (`overlayLockLayerAt`) reads every active environment row and takes the strictest lock among the rows in scope (`:10048`), so a `?package=P` delete of a two-package item is judged on the strictest of both rows: fail-closed, never a bypass, at worst an over-refusal on the other package's `no-delete`. Pre-existing, not a storage-order pick, outside triage's ordered paths — a parity gap the widening left (③), **not wrong**.
13. **The replaced #22128 rider case.** "active, no row at the env-local address: the read serves `null`, and `If-None-Match: *` creates it" pinned the defect itself: a `?package=all` save minting an env-local row beside the package's, with the read serving `null` for a one-package item. The replacement pins the rider's invariant at the resolved address (the read's token is keyed and is what the save compares against; `If-None-Match: *` is refused with it as `currentVersion`; `If-Match` writes the package row), and the empty-address half (`null`, then a create) stays pinned in `meta-item-version-token-occ.test.ts` (#22114). **Right.**
14. **The corrected doubles and the ledger.** The two delete-path doubles now store `package_id: null` as the store does and answer `sys_metadata` finds holding the caller's limit; no assertion moved. The engine-double ledger records the new file's three pinned verbs. **Right.**
15. **Check-runs on the head.** Read 2026-10-13T15:08Z: 40 runs — 31 success, 5 skipped, 4 in progress, 0 failed. The required contexts: `Lint & Repo Gates` success, `TypeScript Type Check` success, `Build Core` success, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` success; `Test Core` shards (1/6) in_progress, (2/6) in_progress, (3/6) success, (4/6) in_progress, (5/6) success, (6/6) in_progress. Skipped (path-filtered or opt-in): `Dogfood Verify CLI`, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, `Console Pin Gate`, `Dogfood Regression Gate (matrix/3)`, `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)`. Still in progress: `Test Core (1/6)`, `Test Core (2/6)`, `Test Core (4/6)`, `Test Core (6/6)` — reported as such, not assumed; the seat reads them before landing. Nothing is red at this read.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/23165-direct-save-resolves-package.md` declares `@objectstack/metadata-protocol: minor`, `@objectstack/spec: minor`, `@objectstack/rest: minor`, with `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` at a line start; the PR body carries the same line at line 2 (`Check Changeset` success on the head, so the one reader took it).

- **`Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` — right.** The diff widens a published surface (a new request key on `DeleteMetaItemRequest`, `?package=` on the reset door, the 409 → 200 flip of ①.4a) and narrows two doors' accept sets (①.3, ①.5, ①.4b–c), so the value is `yes` and the arm is the breaking one. The breaking carriers are present: the BREAKING banner, the FROM → TO mapping with the one-line remedy (name the package with `?package=`, and the receipt text a text-comparing client should expect), and the ADR-0087 disposition `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` — honest, since no authorable spelling, export or stored shape is removed, renamed or re-shaped and no stored row is rewritten, so `objectstack migrate meta` has nothing to rewrite and the remedy lives in the request. `check:adr-0087-registration` rides `Lint & Repo Gates`, success.
- **`@objectstack/metadata-protocol` `minor` — right.** `deleteMetaItem` is a public method on the exported class and its request widens; the doors' behaviour narrows; a breaking change ships as `minor` under the launch-window convention `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` states in its header.
- **`@objectstack/spec` `minor` — right** (the resume had `patch`): `DeleteMetaItemRequestSchema.packageId` is a new optional key on a published request payload (`DeleteMetaItemRequest` is its `z.input`, and `MetadataProtocol.deleteMetaItem` types against it), the clause-② shape; the two describes are text.
- **`@objectstack/rest` `minor` — right.** The reset door accepts a new parameter, and `META_ITEM_RESET_PARAMS` is an exported constant whose value grows.
- Nothing else publishes: `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json` and `content/docs/references/` are not packages; no `skip-changeset`. The level axis (a clause-② PR grades at least one moved package `minor` or above) holds three times over.

### ③ Boundary flags

`open_questions`: none in report `6148282605`. Each `deviations` entry, each `out_of_scope_findings` entry, each acceptance note, and what the ACCEPT (`6148342520`) handed this review:

- **D1, the file surface widened to `rest-server.ts`, `DeleteMetaItemRequestSchema`, `deletePackage` and the draft discards.** Answered in ①.6–7: necessary, proportionate, the save's grammar, inside triage's delete-door direction; `packages/rest` stays with the claiming seat under this review as the ACCEPT ruled; the commits are separated (`3b0118f85`, `ddf0177ef`). Answered.
- **D2, test files outside `metadata-protocol/src`.** The pins sit where the doors are: the real routes and the request schema. Answered.
- **D3, `spec` and `rest` graded `minor`.** Answered in ②.
- **D4, lock-queue timeouts and background waits.** Process; no bearing.
- **OOS1, S6 reachable through today's doors** (an unbound row stored first, then a package-naming save beside it; the read naming no package keeps serving the unbound row while the package-less save writes the package's row). Correctly outside this PR: the producer is the package-naming save beside an unbound row, the card's existing-rows line forbids conversion, and ADR-0048 §3.3's first-match read is the contract it rides. The ACCEPT says the cards are "filed in the next comment"; at this read (card comments through `6148342520`, PR comments through the drift check) no such comment exists. **ESCALATED to the seat**: file the S6 card before landing, so the defect is carried and not buried.
- **OOS2, plugin-security's by-name deletes now 409 on a name two packages hold; `storedRowPackageArg` (#21861) becomes redundant.** Carrier named; answered. The same card should name the runtime's flow registration door (①.11), which the report's three runtime consumer files (packaged-base lock, read-your-writes, uninstall org scope) do not cover by name. That card is likewise not yet on the thread.
- **OOS3, the SDK's `meta.deleteItem` and the console's reset send no package.** Console: objectstack-ai/objectui#12300. SDK: the ACCEPT promised a card, and none is on the thread yet — the same escalation as OOS1.
- **Acceptance note, the registry heal after a delete that leaves another row stored — ESCALATED (pre-existing, not a condition of this PR).** `restoreArtifactRegistryView` runs on every active delete whatever remains; its tiers heal the runtime shadow, re-register a packaged artifact or, on a control-plane kernel only, a MetadataService baseline, and retire a name no layer serves — none re-registers a remaining `sys_metadata` row. So after `?package=P` on a two-package runtime-only item the registry retires the entry while the store still holds Q's row: persisted state and runtime state disagree until the next hydration or save. The store-backed doors are pinned (the protocol read and the real `GET` serve Q); the registry-backed ones (ObjectQL `getObject` and data CRUD for an `object`, registry lookups) are not — the dev says NOT MEASURED, carrier none. The same end state was reachable at base (a package-less delete of a two-package item ran the same heal), and triage's direction does not name the registry, so it is not a condition here; but a note with no carrier on a store/registry disagreement is the quiet direction. Measure it on a real kernel (an `object` two packages hold, `?package=P`, then the data door), and if the registry drops the item, re-hydrate the remaining served row inside the heal, or file it as class (a) with a carrier.
- **Acceptance note, the draft save with two packages binds by storage order (`resolveWriteHead`, #11087).** Unchanged per triage; the describe's "the package the item's active row is bound to" is true for one package and silent for two. Not a condition; the same class as this card's refusal, for a follow-up card when measured.

- **Acceptance note, `os migrate security-catalog-overlays`.** A two-package group would be refused where it drained; its integration test holds none and is declared to CI. Consistent with the direction; answered.
